subject: Materials Science
title: Magnetic Particle Inspection
description: A 60-second lesson on Magnetic Particle Inspection.

hook.text: Sprinkle iron powder on a magnetized steel part — the powder clusters around cracks like iron filings on a magnet.

buildup.text: A surface or near-surface crack disrupts the magnetic field, creating flux leakage that attracts particles.

discovery.text: Fluorescent magnetic particles under UV light make even hairline cracks glow bright green.

twist.text: MPI only works on ferromagnetic materials — aluminum, copper, and stainless steel need other methods.

climax.text: Crankshafts, axles, and rail wheels are MPI-checked routinely — fast, cheap, and highly sensitive.

punchline.text: Magnetize, sprinkle, and inspect — cracks reveal themselves in glowing lines.

quiz.question: What limits magnetic particle inspection?
options: It only works on ferromagnetic materials
It can only detect deep internal defects
